title: llm-api-rapid-rebuttal-grid
summary: One-page rapid rebuttal grid for SDRs/AE field use: slices competitive conversations into 6 tradeoff axes, gives short proof points, demo hooks, and escalation guidance. Meant to be memorized or kept in browser for quick responses during discovery or objections calls.
audience: AEs, SDRs, Solutions Engineers, Sales Engineers who need a fast, repeatable way to counter common vendor claims from other LLM API providers.
format_notes: Not a legal doc or pricing sheet — use alongside product demo + pricing. Keep responses concise (<30s). When in doubt, offer a follow-up deep-dive with an SE and reference the sandbox or dedicated latency report.
competitive_axes: Performance (latency / cost per token) | Redwood strength: production-optimized runtime, cross-model kernel selection & continuous batching reduces p95 by 20-40% on common workloads. | Typical competitor claim: "'we have faster inference'" | Rapid rebuttal: cite our p95 benchmarks for NER/chat at 128/512 tokens; mention autoscaling + dynamic batching lowers unit cost without burdening devs. | Demo hook: show live latency dashboard and per-route token cost in Console.

Deployment flexibility | Redwood strength: same API for hosted, dedicated, and private VPC/on-prem with consistent rollouts. | Competitor claim: "we offer both hosted and private too" | Rebuttal: emphasize control plane parity — private gets same rollout/observability primitives; competitor often lacks feature parity or requires heavy integration work. | Demo: quick tour of Console showing identical route config between hosted and private stubs.

Observability & debugability | Redwood: token-level traces, route/model cost breakdown, prompt diffing + retrievable past requests for regression analysis. | Competitor claim: "we provide logs/metrics" | Rebuttal: many vendors expose coarse metrics only; call out our model-level A/B dashboards and alerting tied to eval sets. | Demo: show trace for a slow request, jump from sample to model version diff.

Reliability & graceful degradation | Redwood: smart routing + automatic fallback model variants, regional fallback and throttling policies. | Competitor claim: "we have retries" | Rebuttal: retries can inflate cost & latency; our routing policies avoid retries by intelligently falling back to compatible variants with similar semantics. | Demo: simulate a degraded instance and show auto-failover in Console timeline.

Enterprise controls & compliance | Redwood: private deploy option, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC-level controls. | Competitor claim: "we're enterprise ready" | Rebuttal: ask about private control plane parity, key management options, and audit retention windows — most competitors require bespoke work. | Demo: show audit log entry + KMS config page.

Developer experience & MTTI (time-to-first-success) | Redwood: SDKs, quickstart templates, sample prompt presets, and unbiased performance profiles in model catalog. | Competitor claim: "we're easy to use" | Rebuttal: ask for a sample app or template for the customer's exact flow; highlight our templates for chat, search, reranking which shave weeks off integration. | Demo: spin up sample repo and run the quickstart (3-minute flow).
one_liners: If latency matters, show them our p95 dashboards — numbers beat buzzwords.
We don't force a model or infra bet; we give the same interface whether hosted, dedicated, or private.
Retries are a band-aid; routing+fallbacks are the surgery — that's where we win on SLOs and cost.
Ask early about audit/KMS needs — many vendors only add that once contracts start, but it's built into our Private story.
Developer ergonomics win deals — offer a quickstart and the customer can judge integration effort themselves.
objection_handling: Objection: 'Their price per token is lower.' Suggested response: 'What's the typical input/output length and concurrency for your use case? Lower list prices often break when you add retries, longer contexts, or when throughput matters — we optimize unit economics across those axes and can model it for you during POC.'

Objection: 'They already have an enterprise contract.' Suggested response: 'Are you tied to a specific SLA or feature set in that contract? We often win on operational predictability and lower cost at scale; propose a limited Dedicated pilot comparing identical workload traces.'

Objection: 'We need air-gapped/on-prem.' Suggested response: 'We support private deployments with a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package. We can start with a VPC install and plan a staged air-gap if needed — let's scope the compliance checklist together.'

Objection: 'Their model is higher quality for our vertical.' Suggested response: 'Quality is workload-dependent; let's run a short eval on your prompt set and tie regressions to alerts. If needed we can suggest model variants or quantization profiles that preserve quality while cutting cost.'
demo_hooks: Latency + cost tour: live p95 timeline, then switch to per-route token-cost view to show tradeoffs.
Private parity demo: flip between hosted and private view in Console to show identical rollout controls.
Regression guardrail: show an eval tied to a production prompt set that triggers a quality alert and a canary rollback.
Failure simulation: trigger a degraded worker and show graceful fallback in the request timeline.
escalation_playbook: Tier 1: SE joins for a deeper technical comparison (topology, KMS, VPC network flow). Use the sandbox + customer's sample traces.
Tier 2: Solutions Eng + Infra engineer for a Dedicated sizing and cost modeling session; produce commit-level throughput estimates and expected p95 under target concurrency.
Tier 3: Legal/security sync for Private/on-prem agreements — surface SOC/ISO artifacts, define audit log retention and KMS requirements.
risks_and_open_questions: Confirm customer's concurrency profile and 95th percentile latency target — many 'price' objections evaporate once we model real traffic.
If competitor claims 'same feature parity' ask for one specific feature (e.g., per-token traces) and request a proof point or screenshot.
Check procurement timelines for enterprise customers — Private deployments can be scheduled to align with procurement milestones to avoid stalling the deal.
